requirements.requirement: Add at least 512 MB of compressed in-memory swap on node1
requirements.summary: A zram0 device was created with disksize 536870912 bytes (512 MiB) and comp_algorithm lzo, then formatted with mkswap and activated via swapon, confirmed present in /proc/swaps and zramctl output as a 512M lzo-compressed swap device.

requirements.requirement: zram swap active at boot (persists across restart)
requirements.summary: A systemd oneshot unit (zram-swap.service, RemainAfterExit=yes) was created and enabled for multi-user.target and swap.target. The executor captured a pre-reboot baseline (boot_id 0d6209e2..., zram active/enabled), issued a real reboot, waited through a connection timeout, reconnected with a new boot_id (b8697ca4...), and confirmed zram0 was again active, enabled, and correctly sized/compressed post-restart — a full bounded disruption-and-recovery transition.

requirements.requirement: zram swap preferred over any disk-backed swap
requirements.summary: /proc/swaps shows /dev/zram0 at priority 100 versus /dev/vda2 (disk-backed) at priority -2, both immediately after setup and again after the real reboot, demonstrating zram is preferred in both the pre- and post-restart state.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task — adding 512 MB of lzo-compressed zram swap, making it persist across boot, and giving it priority over disk-backed swap — are directly and coherently evidenced, including a real reboot with a verified boot_id change and confirmed post-restart recovery of the zram swap at the correct priority and size. Hygiene is good: a brief troubleshooting cycle (modprobe/swapoff/rmmod) was fully reverted, and the only residue is a small /tmp/reboot.log file left from capturing the restart, which is low-risk and incidental to legitimate evidence collection.
limitations: Package-health checks were unavailable (timed out) both before and after, so native package-manager consistency could not be independently confirmed.
/tmp/reboot.log remains on node1; it is minor and low-risk but was not cleaned up after use.

operational_hygiene.summary: The command sequence shows a bounded troubleshooting cycle: modprobe zram + manual comp_algorithm check (cmd-905ca544e0474525), followed by swapoff -a and rmmod zram (cmd-6f57b0d13d6b48fd) to reset state before building the permanent systemd unit. This experiment was fully reverted — disk swap was restored via 'swapon -a' inside cmd-71657b7cd6ac4620, and zram was rebuilt cleanly through the new service, so no lasting damage or conflicting state resulted. The reboot command redirected output to /tmp/reboot.log (cmd-1d40c588e3e2464d), which remains on node1 per the after_executor temporary-files snapshot — a minor, low-risk residue that was a necessary side effect of capturing the async reboot rather than an unrelated mutation. No failed services, package damage, or new listening sockets were introduced; socket/PID differences between snapshots are attributable to the reboot itself, not new exposure.
